title: Why Sanitary Tees Fail on Horizontal Drainage
description: Installing a standard sanitary tee on its side in horizontal drain lines is a widespread installation error. Sanitary tees feature a short radius turn designed strictly for transitioning from horizontal to vertical flow. When used horizontally, the sharp turn fails to direct wastewater smoothly, leading to sluggish flow, frequent blockages, and poor solid transport. Plumbing codes mandate long-sweep combination wyes or 1/8 bends with a wye for horizontal branch connections. Correct fitting selection ensures proper fluid velocity, prevents waste buildup, and maintains system self-cleansing action. Always verify fitting orientation against your local plumbing code before glueing.

Why Sanitary Tees Fail on Horizontal Drainage

Installing a standard sanitary tee on its side in horizontal drain lines is a widespread installation error. Sanitary tees feature a short radius turn designed strictly for transitioning from horizontal to vertical flow. When used horizontally, the sharp turn fails to direct wastewater smoothly, leading to sluggish flow, frequent blockages, and poor solid transport. Plumbing codes mandate long-sweep combination wyes or 1/8 bends with a wye for horizontal branch connections. Correct fitting selection ensures proper fluid velocity, prevents waste buildup, and maintains system self-cleansing action. Always verify fitting orientation against your local plumbing code before glueing.
